reason:
Reproduced exactly, on both grounds, by driving 1440x960 owner-flight and harvesting .b-stamp before and after each of the six mutations. paper and ink are identical: move +7 -> "Updated 15 July 2026" (readout moved to Saturday 8 August, in 23 days); typed date "20 August 2026" -> "Updated 15 July 2026"; rename -> "Updated 15 July 2026"; hide -> "Updated 15 July 2026"; delete -> "Updated 15 July 2026"; add -> "Updated 16 July 2026". Deleting six of the seven forward moments one after another left the footer still reading "Updated 15 July 2026" with one moment remaining. The code reading is exact: F.updatedLabel has three writers (render-b.js:1260 in the add branch, 1589 in the owner-draft state, 1660 on the first-run path) and none of them is the one function all six mutations pass through - grep confirms exactly six remember(root, ...) call sites (914, 942, 974, 1074, 1231, 1269) against one definition at 637, and paintPublication:1099-1100 is the only thing that writes the node. The add branch's own comment states the rule the other five break.

All four refuting angles fail. (1) NOT the round-7 item. freshness-stamp-is-decoration was killed on co-visibility: "Live since 15 July" at y=191 versus the stamp at y=1998, ~1800px apart, different registers, so "the same date twice" rested on a proximity that does not exist. That objection is untouched here because this is a claim about the VALUE being false, not the string being redundant, and the reader is the guest. Measured on the guest desk at 1440: .b-stamp is at y=1561, visibility visible, and a full-page scan of body text returns exactly one freshness string - ["Updated 15 July 2026"]. .b-shared does not exist on that surface. Same on phone and print. So on the guest surfaces the stamp is not one of two freshness claims, it is the only one, and round 7's kill has no purchase. (2) The stamp IS the guest's, and the staleness reaches them in-session. The fixture derives live() on call precisely so owner edits reach the guest states (fixture.js:110-114), and [data-act="preview"] (render-b.js:1296) walks the owner straight to the guest desk. Driven: owner moves the first moment +14, presses Done, presses Preview - the guest row goes from "16 days away ... Sat 1 Aug" to "30 days away ... Sat 15 Aug" while the footer still reads "Updated 15 July 2026". Delete then Preview: 7 owner rows become 6 guest rows, the deleted id is gone, stamp still "Updated 15 July 2026". The guest is shown a changed plan under an eleven-day-old date, with nothing else on the surface to correct it. (3) "Updated" is a content claim, not a publication one, by the artifact's own construction. If it meant publication it would not move on add either - the add branch's comment says in as many words that the publication record does NOT move when a moment is added, and moves the stamp anyway. owner-draft, a plan nobody holds, still renders "Updated 16 July 2026". So the semantics are settled inside the artifact and five of six content changes break them. (4) Not per-keystroke. remember fires on the title field's change, not its input: typing 13 characters produced an empty undo bar during typing, one entry ("Renamed to Dress fitting.") on commit, and one press of Undo emptied the stack. One write per committed, reversible change, and the value written is a date, so repeated writes inside a day produce a byte-identical string - no churn to see.

The fix breaks neither gate. The two stamp-adjacent assertions are interaction-check.mjs:2297 (the morning) and 2322 (an empty project), and both surfaces pass foot({stamp:false}): driven, .b-stamp is null on day, owner-empty, publish, ended and loading. paintPublication already guards with if (stamp), and remember is not reachable on any of them. The fix is a correction inside a frozen structure, roughly two lines moved, and it closes the hole the gate already fences on both sides.
sharpenedFix: As proposed, with three refinements. (a) Put the pair at the TOP of remember (render-b.js:637), before entry.at = window.scrollY, not merely before paintUndo - the scroll capture can be reordered later and the stamp write should not depend on where it sits relative to it. (b) Keep paintPublication as the single writer rather than touching .b-stamp directly, so the "one writer" rule at 1087 survives; F.publication is untouched by every mutation, so repainting .b-shared and the primary verb on each change is a provable no-op. (c) When deleting 1260-1261 from the add branch, carry the first sentence of its comment with the code - "The stamp moves, because the plan just changed" belongs on remember now, and the remainder ("The publication record does NOT ... cannot un-hand it to them") must stay in the add branch, because that half is about F.publication and is still only true there. Leave undo alone as the finding says. Add one gate assertion to interaction-check.mjs alongside 2297/2322 that drives one move and one delete on owner-flight and asserts .b-stamp reads today on both grounds, so the sixth branch cannot drift back out.
